$comment: The spend-based circuit breaker for the research lane (#2946, requested by Eric 2026-09-16 as a stopgap ahead of the batching/model-tier redesign). Distinct from research-dispatch-budget.json (per-tick session COUNT) and the held research-daily-budget.json (rolling session COUNT): this is keyed to actual measured total_cost_usd, because a count-based cap can still be blindsided by one anomalously expensive session. Same fail-closed doctrine as the other budget files — a missing or malformed threshold refuses to dispatch rather than defaulting to unlimited.
$why: Eric picked A2 on #6020 (2026-11-01): $100 per 4h at halt, conserve and normal, $200 while the work-mode dial reads surge. Sized from 187 real ticks 2026-10-12..26 and recounted to 2026-10-30, not guessed: the highest 4h spend was $51.35 at normal, $64.36 at conserve, $104.42 at surge, and $83.37 at normal on 2026-10-30 (a backlog release after 75.8 quiet hours, which fired the 10-26 falsifier and moved the predicted $80/$160 to $100/$200). Replayed, these lines trip on 0 of those ticks; a 108-session runaway is about $105 and still trips at normal. One line for every mode but surge because spend per 4h follows how often ticks run, not legs per tick (10-16, under conserve, was the dearest day at $124.11), so scaling by the research cap would have tripped 59 conserve ticks. History: the 2026-09-17 canary was $15 per 4h (shrunk from an unvalidated 150/24h under Opus-era assumptions) and never counted a dollar, because its pattern wanted the ::notice:: form the workflow writes and the log GitHub serves back says ##[notice] (#4437, #6020). Dollars are the CLI imputed API-equivalent under the Max 20 flat fee, not a literal charge; a first reading puts a weekly-quota point at about $16 to $24 (a floor, cloud sessions uncounted). Falsifier (#6020, dated 2026-11-09): a non-surge 4h window over $100 that nobody calls a runaway moves the line again, and a dispatch-run window over its mode line that did not trip is a counting bug.
$mechanism: Unlike the count-based caps, this cannot be computed from local git history alone — it reads real spend from recent GitHub Actions run logs and a durable, human-clearable state carried as a GitHub issue label (never a committed file, since this repo's research lane never pushes to main directly outside a PR — issue #915, Eric 2026-08-30). Once tripped: the label goes on trackingIssue and STAYS until a human removes it — dispatch returns empty on every subsequent tick regardless of what the rolling window recomputes to, by design (fail-hard, not fail-slow: a self-healing rolling cap would silently reopen once the expensive burst aged out of the window, which is exactly the behavior Eric asked NOT to have).
